 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction

 Vs.
The State of Maharashtra and Others ...Respondents

Mr. Rajesh Mali, PSI, Baramati Police Station, Present.
 CORAM:- N. J. JAMADAR, J.
 DATED:- 14th DECEMBER, 2023 P.C:-
1) Heard the learned Counsel for the applicant and the learned APP for the State.

2) This application is preferred for pre-arrest bail  connection with C.R. No. 873 of 2023, registered with Baramati Police Station, Pune for the offences punishable under Sections 376 (2)(n), 376(d), 294 (b), 354(a), 354(b), 354(d) 327, 323, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("the Dattatray Shankar Sonawane vs State Of Maharashtra on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13634272/

sentences.text: The first informant is a married lady.
She claimed to have become acquainted with the applicant in the month of November, 2022 on Instagram.

The applicant had allegedly forced her to share her mobile number and, thereafter,
developed proximity with her.
4) The first informant alleges that the applicant took her to various places and made her consume liquor and sexually exploited her without her consent.
Various instances of the applicant resorting to abuses and violence to allegedly force her to give in to his lust have been adverted to in the FIR.
5) On 8th November, 2023 the applicant allegedly abused and assaulted the first informant in the presence of his friends.
The applicant had checked the mobile phone of the first informant.
She was abused for having illicit relations with others.
First informant's friend - Vikas rescued her from the applicant and called the husband of the first informant and, thereafter, they approached the police station and lodged the report.
6) The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the first informant and the applicant are both married.
They have been in a relationship outside their respective marriages since more than a year.

Attention of the Court was invited to the Dattatray Shankar Sonawane vs State Of Maharashtra on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13634272/

sentences.text: 7) The learned APP resisted the prayer for pre-arrest bail.
It was submitted that the allegations in the FIR indicate that the applicant never gave consent for sexual relations and the applicant coerced her to meet his demand by threats and violence.

The learned APP further submitted that in view of the further statement of the first informant including her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 before the learned Magistrate, offence under Section 376D of the Penal Code has also been added.

In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of the Code, 1973, the victim had, inter alia, alleged that on 8th November, 2023, the applicant and his friends had abducted her in a four wheeler and the applicant and his friends had sexually exploited her.
8) I have perused the allegations in the FIR and the material on record including the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of the Code, 1973.

 910-ABA-3508-23.DOC conversation placed on record by the applicant, it prima facie appears that the applicant and the first informant were in a relationship outside marriage.
There is material to show that the victim had accompanied the applicant to far off places on multiple occasions and stayed overnight.
It is true the victim has alleged that she was forced to accompany the applicant.
However, the relationship seems to have lasted for more than a year.
In the circumstances, till the application is heard finally after providing an opportunity to the victim, it may be expedient to protect the liberty of the applicant.
9) Hence, the following order:-
ORDER I) The applicant shall amend the application to implead the victim as party respondent no. 2 by concealing her identity.
II) Necessary amendment be carried out forthwith.
III) Issue notice to the respondents, returnable on 18 th January. 2024.
IV) Smt. Takalkar, the learned APP waives notice for respondent no.1/State.

V) In addition to notice through Court, the Investigating Officer shall serve the respondent No. 2 and file a report.
910-ABA-3508-23.DOC

VI ) In the meanwhile, in the event of arrest of the applicant in connection with C.R. No. 873 of 2023, registered with Baramati Police Station, Pune for the offences punishable under Sections 376 (2)(n), 376(d), 294 (b), 354(a), 354(b), 354(d) 327, 323, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860, the applicant be released on bail on executing a PR Bond in the sum of Rs.30,000/-with one or two sureties in the like amount.

VII) The applicant shall co-operate with the investigation and attend Baramati Police Station, Pune on 22nd,26th and 27th December, 2023 in between 10.00 am to 1.00 pm and, thereafter, as and when directed by the Investigating Officer.
VIII) The applicant shall not enter the limits of Baramati except for the purpose of attending the proceedings before the Court or Baramati Police Station.
